- **Does not answer:** Which mandatory rule of the applicable law lays down a limitation period of its own? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART10_1_EN). THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).
- **Does not answer:** What does the 1980 UN Convention answer on limitation? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART10_2_EN). THE 1980 UN CONVENTION HAS NO SUCH CHAPTER AT ALL: limitation is outside its subject matter and lives in the separate 1974 New York Convention. There is no bridge to `intl.uncitral.cisg*` here in substance, not for want of work.
- **Does not answer:** Which days are counted in the period and are any of them non-business days? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART10_2_EN). THE COUNT BEGINS ON THE NEXT DAY, AND THE TEXT SAYS SO: "beginning on the day after the day…" in both parts of article 10.2. The §86 policy of the package is `start_count next_day`, so a three-year period from 10 March 2020 expires on 11 March 2023 and not on the 10th. The Principles have no calendar of business days: the periods are calendar periods.
- **Does not answer:** What are the periods in years as agreed by the parties? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART10_3_EN). THE THREE LIMITS ON MODIFYING THE PERIODS (article 10.3) ARE PRESENTED AS FACTS OF THE CASE: whether the general period has been shortened to less than one year, the maximum period to less than four years, or extended to more than fifteen. The model does not compute the comparisons itself, because the agreed periods arrive as data.

| `limitation-suspended` | Is the running of the limitation period suspended (art. 10.5–10.8)? | truth | `limitation_suspended(r: Right)` | `evaluate truth(limitation_suspended(r: <r>));` | Article 10.7. Articles 10.5 and 10.6 apply with appropriate modifications to proceedings whereby the parties request a third person to assist them in reaching an amicable settlement (`SuspensionByAmicableSettlementProceedings`); Article 10.6(1). The running of the limitation period is suspended when the obligee performs an act recognised by the law of the arbitral tribunal as asserting its right (`SuspensionByArbitralAct`); Article 10.5(1)(c). The running of the limitation period is suspended where the obligee has asserted its rights in proceedings for dissolution of the obligor (`SuspensionByDissolutionClaim`); Article 10.8(2). Where the impediment consists of the incapacity or death of a party, suspension ceases when a representative or successor has been appointed; the additional one-year period applies accordingly (`SuspensionByIncapacityEndsOnAppointment`); Article 10.5(1)(b). The running of the limitation period is suspended where the obligee has asserted its rights in the insolvency proceedings (`SuspensionByInsolvencyClaim`); Article 10.5(1)(a). The running of the limitation period is suspended when the obligee performs an act recognised by the law of the court as asserting its right (`SuspensionByJudicialAct`) | tests 1 |

- **Does not answer:** How many days of the period remain after the suspension has ended? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART10_5_EN, PICC_ART10_8_EN). SUSPENSION IS A FACT OF THE CASE HERE, NOT A COMPUTATION: the model answers whether the running of the period is suspended and the day before which it cannot expire, but does not recompute the remainder of the period by the days of suspension — the source gives no such rule, and inventing arithmetic for it is not permitted.
- **Does not answer:** Does the law of the court or of the arbitral tribunal treat this act as asserting the right? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART10_5_EN, PICC_ART10_6_EN). WHAT COUNTS AS ASSERTING A RIGHT IN PROCEEDINGS IS DECIDED BY THE LAW OF THE COURT OR THE ARBITRAL TRIBUNAL (articles 10.5, 10.6): this is a direct reference outwards, and it enters the model as a fact of the case.
